title: A total wrong only for a quote no constructor makes, proved only on the quotes the constructor makes
summary: The value-object refactor of 190, with `total` returning a wrong amount for a quantity of zero or less, which `Quote`'s constructor refuses. The tool proves `total` preserved, and its result says over what: quotes made by their constructor, from any arguments it accepts. The bug is outside that claim, and the claim says it is.

change.description: `Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version `total` also returns `gross + 1` when `q.quantity <= 0`.

risk: A proof over objects has to make them somehow. Made by their constructors, they can't reach every state a field-by-field object could, so a bug only in such a state is not found, and a verdict that didn't say how its inputs were made would read as covering it.
explanation: The check makes each `Quote` by its constructor from symbolic arguments, and its domain label says exactly that: `a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts`, with the old version's quote made from the same values as the correspondence says. The constructor refuses a quantity below 1, so the new branch is never taken in the domain, and the verdict is verified within it, and claimed nowhere else.
resolution: Nothing to fix for a quote made by its constructor. If a `Quote` can reach a quantity below 1 another way (`withQuantity` sets it without a check), the claim doesn't cover it: that is the label's point, and a domain of states after method calls is later work.
notes: Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.

The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the outside-domain defect (`defects/outside-domain/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.

Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.

What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and `Quote#quantity`, whose receiver is made differently in the two versions (`Quote(long, int)` before, `Quote(Money, int)` now), which the regression check doesn't relate yet. Before the application-core merge (2026-11-08) it was refused as an instance method instead; the merge's check takes a receiver made by its constructor, of the same construction in both versions.

Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `Pricing#total` verified, its domain naming the constructor; `POST /quotes`, `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 0.4 s cold, 0.2 s warm.

`withQuantity(q, 0)` gives a quote that this `total` gets wrong, and nothing in the run says otherwise: the kernel's claims are each about one method over constructor-made inputs, not about sequences of calls.
The app's tests pass on this version: the route makes every quote by the constructor.
provenance: Constructed for Phase 5 of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md` (the joint example, made an example under the numbers 190-199). Examples 190 to 196 share the refactor: 190 is the refactor alone, and 191 to 196 each add one of the fixture's defects to it.

references.title: Godlin and Strichman, Regression verification: proving the equivalence of similar programs (2013)
Barthe, Crespo and Kunz, Relational verification using product programs (2011)
